transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I keep getting these really nagging thoughts lately. I work as a designer, and I'll just suddenly worry that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I accidentally sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And even when I look at it and I can see it’s probably fine, my mind just... it keeps circling back to it anyway.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, counting, or going through specific mental steps—to try to reduce the anxiety these thoughts cause?

Yeah, I do. Before I submit my work now, I'll... well, I'll re-open the file just to be sure. I go in and compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes I just mentally walk through every single design choice I made one more time. It doesn't take over my whole day or anything, but it definitely makes me slower. I just feel a lot less free creatively when I have to keep doing all that before I can actually send something out.
When you go through those steps to check your work, do you feel like you have to do them in a very specific way or order, or else you get more anxious?

No, not exactly. I mean... I don't really have a strict order I have to follow. It’s not like I have to check the text layers first and then the images every single time, or do it the exact same way. 

It's more just that I have to keep looking at the file until I feel sure I didn't miss anything. Doing it in a different order doesn't really make me more anxious, as long as I actually get through all the checks before I hit send.
Are these nagging thoughts about mistakes in your work something you actively try to suppress or ignore, or do they feel more like normal worries that just won’t let go?

I definitely try to push them away. Like, I'll tell myself, "You checked it, it's fine, just move on." But it doesn't really work. No matter how much I try to ignore them or suppress them, those thoughts just keep popping back up. Like I said before, it's this constant nagging feeling that I missed a tiny mistake or sent the wrong file, and my brain just keeps circling back to it, even when I try to force myself to focus on something else.
Do these thoughts and the checking behaviors you described cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your work or daily life?

Well, I wouldn't say it's completely taking over my life, but it definitely causes some problems at work. I'm still getting my projects done, but... I've actually started missing some internal deadlines because I spend so much extra time checking everything. 

And, honestly, it's affecting my actual designs, too. I find myself holding back on bolder ideas because I'm just so afraid I'll overlook a mistake in a complex file. It's really frustrating because I've been trying to position myself for a creative director role, and I feel like this constant second-guessing is going to damage my chances of moving up. So, yeah, it is causing me some distress, for sure.

Have you noticed these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors happening in situations outside of your work, like at home or in your personal life, or do they seem to be limited mostly to when you're working?

No, not really. It seems to just be a work thing. I mean, at home, I might double-check that the front door is locked or something, but it's just a normal quick check, nothing like what happens with my design files. The really intense worrying and the constant checking... that's pretty much just limited to my job and my projects.
Have you ever had intrusive thoughts or felt the need to check things repeatedly outside of work, even if only occasionally, such as concerns about germs, orderliness, or safety?

No, I really haven't. Like I said, it's pretty much just a work thing. I don't worry about germs or keeping things perfectly organized at home, and I don't have any major safety concerns either. It's just the design files and my projects at work that get me stuck in that loop.
When you're not actively checking your work, do you still feel anxious or distressed about the possibility of having made a mistake?

Um, yes, I do. Even when I'm not actively looking at the files, I still feel this sort of lingering anxiety. It's like a background noise, just this nagging feeling that I might have missed something important. So, yeah, the worry doesn't just turn off when I step away from the computer.
Have you ever had intrusive, unwanted thoughts, images, or urges that caused you significant anxiety or distress, even if they weren't related to your work or design files?

No, honestly, I haven't. Like I mentioned, it really is just focused on my job. I mean, that's the whole reason I came in—I just keep getting these nagging thoughts that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I’ve sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And even when I look at it and I can see it’s probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it. But outside of that? No, I don't have any disturbing images or urges or anything like that in my personal life.
How much time do you spend each day going through these checking rituals or dealing with these intrusive thoughts about your work?

It doesn't take over my whole day, but it definitely adds up. Um, before I submit any work now, I’ll re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and... sometimes I just mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. 

So time-wise, it might just be an extra twenty or thirty minutes a day of actually doing those checks, but the main thing is that it just makes me slower overall. I feel a lot less free creatively because I'm always second-guessing it.
